title: Copilot Studio: express mode speeds up flows called by an agent or app
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, maker setting, administrator controls and documented limits are supported. It correctly distinguishes the preview documentation from the roadmap target and explains that express mode adds no surcharge while flow actions remain metered.

claims.claim: The record lists Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365) and Microsoft Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes faster flow runs and fewer timeout interruptions for agents and apps.
claims.quote: Express mode ensures agents and apps receive timely and reliable responses by dramatically accelerating flow run times. This reduces flow failures, improves user experience, and eliminates costly interruptions caused by timeout issues.

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-07-10T21:58:35.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Express mode can speed up agent flows and help them respond within the two-minute window.
claims.quote: When you use express mode, your flow can achieve faster execution times. This feature increases the likelihood that agent flows can complete within the two-minute window and provide a response in time.

claims.claim: Express mode supports flows using the When an agent calls a flow trigger.
claims.quote: The flow must have either the When an agent calls a flow or the When an app calls a flow trigger.

claims.claim: Express mode supports flows using the When an app calls a flow trigger.
claims.quote: The flow must have either the When an agent calls a flow or the When an app calls a flow trigger.

claims.claim: A Response action, Respond to agent or Respond to app, is required.
claims.quote: The flow must have a Response action, either Respond to agent or Respond to app.

claims.where: licensing.notes; What's changing; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: Express mode is available only for flows with a Copilot Studio plan associated.
claims.quote:
The flow must have a Copilot Studio plan associated with it.
Express mode is available only for flows under the Copilot Studio plan.

claims.claim: The Power Automate environment must use the new infrastructure.
claims.quote: The Power Automate environment must be on new infrastructure. See Availability for more information.

claims.where: summary; controls[0].note; What's changing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Learn documents express mode as preview and warns that the documentation may change.
claims.quote: This article contains Microsoft Copilot Studio preview documentation and is subject to change.

claims.claim: Without express mode, the documented response timeout for agent- or app-initiated flows is two minutes.
claims.quote: By default, an agent or app initiates an agent flow that fails if it takes longer than two minutes to respond to the calling agent or app.

claims.claim: Express mode flows must still complete within two minutes or time out.
claims.quote: When you turn on express mode, flows must complete in two minutes. Flows that take longer time out.

claims.claim: The per-flow maker path is Flows > flow > Overview > Details > Edit > Express mode.
claims.quote:
Select Flows, and then select the flow for which you want to turn on express mode.
In the Details section of the Overview page, select Edit.
The Details panel appears.
Turn on Express mode. The toggle is at the bottom of the panel.

claims.claim: The toggle is also available on the supported trigger card in the flow designer.
claims.quote: You can also turn on express mode from the When an agent calls a flow or the When an app calls a flow trigger itself while you're building the flow in the designer on the trigger card.

claims.where: controls[0].api; controls[0].note; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No API for the express mode toggle is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: '"express mode" "API" "workflow"'; '"express mode" "Power Platform" "PowerShell" "admin"'. Opened agent-flow-express-mode; no toggle API found.

claims.where: controls[1]; summary; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: No tenant-wide or environment-level administrator switch specifically for express mode is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio express mode default enabled tenant environment administrator switch API Power Platform Dataverse workflow express mode toggle; '"express mode" "Power Platform" "PowerShell" "admin"'. Opened agent-flow-express-mode; only a per-flow toggle found.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The user-opt-in classification describes a capability makers choose per flow, with no documented administrator enablement switch.
claims.quote:
Select Flows, and then select the flow for which you want to turn on express mode.
Turn on Express mode. The toggle is at the bottom of the panel.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the toggle's default on arrival or its general availability default.
claims.quote: Searched: '"express mode" "default" "Copilot"'; Copilot Studio express mode default enabled tenant environment administrator switch API Power Platform Dataverse workflow express mode toggle. Opened agent-flow-express-mode; no toggle arrival default stated.

claims.claim: No source states that existing flows automatically change behaviour on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: '"express mode" "default" "Copilot"'. Read roadmap record and agent-flow-express-mode; neither states that existing flows automatically enter express mode.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Data-heavy flows can fail under express mode because connector data exceeds its memory limits.
claims.quote:
Large data amounts exceed the memory limit of express mode.
If you encounter a flow runtime error mentioning a data limitation, turn off express mode, and try it with other flows instead.

claims.claim: A flow's response failure affects the calling agent or app.
claims.quote: This failure affects the functionality and usability of the agent or app that calls the flow.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The connector response message size limit is 64 KB per individual action.
claims.quote: The message size limit for data passed in an individual action (connector response) is 64 KB.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Variable content is limited to 1,024 characters.
claims.quote: Variable content limit: 1,024 characters.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Delay actions are unsupported when express mode is on.
claims.quote: Delay and webhook actions in the flow aren't supported when express mode is turned on.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Webhook actions are unsupported when express mode is on.
claims.quote: Delay and webhook actions in the flow aren't supported when express mode is turned on.

claims.claim: Unsupported Delay or webhook actions produce errors when the flow is saved.
claims.quote: Delay and webhook actions in the flow aren't supported when express mode is turned on. Errors appear when saving the flow.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends no more than 100 actions per run as a safe limit, while qualifying that more may work.
claims.quote: 100 actions is a safe limit for flow size. In practice, you might be able to include more than 100 actions, depending on how large the flow is, and on how much data processing the flow does.

claims.claim: Loops count as one action per loop iteration toward the flow action count.
claims.quote: The actions count includes loops, which count as one action for each loop iteration.

claims.claim: An Apply to each loop is limited to 100 array items.
claims.quote: Apply to each loop on an array: max 100 items

claims.claim: A Do until loop is limited to 100 iterations.
claims.quote: Do until loop: max 100 iterations

claims.claim: Automatic flow testing does not work in the flow designer.
claims.quote: Test your flow automatically doesn't work in the flow designer. Testing automatically uses flow resubmit, and flow resubmit can't be used with agent-triggered or app-triggered flows.

claims.claim: Loop iterations may be absent from Run details when a connector response exceeds the memory limit.
claims.quote: Loop iterations don't appear in the Run details view when a connector response exceeds the memory limit.

claims.claim: Live activity does not display while an express mode flow is running.
claims.quote: In Express mode, live activity doesn't display while the flow is running.

claims.claim: Express mode is currently available only in upgraded environments on the new architecture.
claims.quote: Express mode is currently only available only for upgraded environments using the new supported architecture.

claims.claim: Microsoft is upgrading environments to support express mode.
claims.quote: Microsoft is in the process of upgrading environments to support express mode.

claims.claim: The express mode page says no action is needed to upgrade the environment.
claims.quote: You don't need to take any action to upgrade your environment.

claims.claim: Some flows can block an environment architecture upgrade.
claims.quote: Some flows might block environment upgrades.

claims.claim: The architecture page recommends updating flows that block upgrades.
claims.quote: We strongly recommend you update these flows, which unblock environment upgrades.

claims.claim: The architecture page explains checking the environmentFlowHostingType value.
claims.quote:
Press Ctrl + Alt + A to view environment debug info and search for environmentFlowHostingType.
If the value is SelfHostMultiTenant, your environment is already on the new SelfHost Multitenant architecture

claims.claim: Microsoft's availability test is to look for the toggle on a supported flow trigger card; its absence means the environment does not yet support express mode.
claims.quote:
Check for the express mode toggle in the designer on the trigger card.
If express mode doesn't appear, your environment doesn't support this feature yet.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The express mode page describes no new data access.
claims.quote: Searched: '"express mode" "identity" "data" "Copilot"'. Opened agent-flow-express-mode in full; it documents execution, prerequisites and data-size limits, not new data access.

claims.claim: The express mode page does not describe a change to flow connections or execution identity.
claims.quote: Searched: '"express mode" "identity" "data" "Copilot"'; Copilot Studio express mode budget cap billing rate data access identity connections. Opened agent-flow-express-mode in full; no connection or execution-identity change is described.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Running a flow in express mode has no added cost.
claims.quote: There's no added cost to running your flows in this mode.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; cost; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Flow actions remain billed under Copilot Studio metering, supporting the variable cost rating.
claims.quote: You're still billed for the number of actions used under Copilot Studio metering.

claims.claim: Express mode is included with the Copilot Studio plan rather than a separate paid add-on.
claims.quote: Express mode is available only for flows under the Copilot Studio plan. There's no added cost to running your flows in this mode.

claims.claim: The feature's prerequisites name a Copilot Studio plan but no separate express mode licence.
claims.quote:
The flow must have a Copilot Studio plan associated with it.
Express mode is available only for flows under the Copilot Studio plan. There's no added cost to running your flows in this mode.

claims.claim: Agent flow test runs are exempt from agent flow action capacity consumption.
claims.quote: Agent flow runs that the agent starts from the test chat in Copilot Studio and test runs that you start in the flow designer, don't consume capacity for agent flow actions and aren't blocked by enforcement.

claims.claim: Qualifying agent-triggered runs for authenticated Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users have no agent flow action charge.
claims.quote: When a user who is authenticated with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license interacts with an agent, and the agent calls an agent flow that uses the When an agent calls the flow trigger, the agent flow actions are included at no charge.

claims.claim: Runs called by autonomous agents are not covered by the Microsoft 365 Copilot user exemption.
claims.quote: Agent flow runs called by an autonomous agent consume Copilot Credits and are subject to enforcement, even if the users in your organization have Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses.

claims.claim: AI tools inside agent flows are metered separately from agent flow action exemptions.
claims.quote: These exemptions apply to agent flow actions. AI tools that run inside an agent flow, such as prompts, are metered separately.

claims.claim: No separate express mode billing rate is published; the feature uses existing flow action metering.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio express mode budget cap billing rate data access identity connections. Opened agent-flow-express-mode and requirements-messages-management; they document no surcharge and standard agent flow action billing, not a separate express mode rate.

claims.claim: No cap or budget control specific to express mode is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio express mode budget cap billing rate data access identity connections. Opened agent-flow-express-mode and requirements-messages-management; the latter documents general environment capacity controls, not an express-mode-specific budget or cap.

claims.claim: Administrators can disable a whole flow at Manage > Environments > environment > Resources > Flows > flow > Disable.
claims.quote:
In the navigation pane, select Manage.
In the Manage pane, select Environments.
On the Environments page, select an environment.
In the Resources web part, select Flows.
On the Flows page, select the flow you want to manage.
Disable or Enable | Disable or enable the flow.

claims.claim: Disable-AdminFlow -EnvironmentName <environment name> -FlowName <flow name> stops the specified flow using the Power Apps administration PowerShell module.
claims.quote:
Module: Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell Module
Stops the specified flow.
Disable-AdminFlow
    -EnvironmentName <String>
    -FlowName <String>
    [-ApiVersion <String>]

claims.claim: Environment Admin, Global admin or Power Platform admin can manage and disable or enable flows.
claims.quote:
If you're an Environment Admin, Global admin, or Power Platform admin, you can manage the flows created in your organization.
Disable or Enable | Disable or enable the flow.

claims.claim: The existing disable control stops the entire flow rather than switching express mode off.
claims.quote: The Disable-AdminFlow cmdlet stops the specified flow.

claims.claim: The separate standard-harness agent flow tool page gives a 100-second response action limit.
claims.quote: Respond to the agent within the 100-second action limit. Optimize the flow logic, queries, and the amount of data returned so that a typical run is below this limit.

claims.claim: Variable-size or memory-limit failures in express mode tests are likely to recur in production.
claims.quote: Express mode fails during test due to a variable size limit or memory limit. If the flow fails during a test, you're likely to hit these issues when the flow is deployed and run in production.

claims.claim: Runtime error messaging explains failures caused by the documented runtime limits.
claims.quote: The runtime error messaging details why the flow failed if it's due to any of the previously mentioned runtime limitations.

claims.claim: Microsoft advises turning express mode off for flows that encounter data limitation runtime errors.
claims.quote: If you encounter a flow runtime error mentioning a data limitation, turn off express mode, and try it with other flows instead.

claims.claim: The express mode feature page names no administrator role required for its maker toggle.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio express mode default enabled tenant environment administrator switch API Power Platform Dataverse workflow express mode toggle. Opened agent-flow-express-mode in full; its prerequisites and toggle instructions name no administrator role.

claims.claim: The new Power Automate architecture is named SelfHost Multitenant.
claims.quote: Power Automate is upgrading environments to new architecture—SelfHost Multitenant—for better performance and feature support.

claims.claim: The agent flow tool page links its response-limit discussion to the express mode page.
claims.quote: Learn more in [Speed up agent flow execution with express mode](agent-flow-express-mode).
